patients.summary: High school math teacher with recurrent genital HSV on episodic valacyclovir who joins the practice in 2022. Three deliveries follow in consecutive Januaries at an outside hospital: a vaginal birth with a third-degree sphincter injury (2024), a cesarean for active HSV lesions in labor (2025), and a trial of labor after cesarean ending in uterine rupture, emergency repair and transfusion (2026), after the practice last saw her.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT. 29F, teaches math at the high school, here to establish. Prior PCP office closing its adult panel; release signed, chart requested.

Concerns: none acute. Wants a doctor she can reach.

Hx: Genital herpes for years, flares a few times a year at most, usually tingling first. Keeps valacyclovir at home and takes 500 mg twice a day for 3 days when she feels it coming; that has worked well. Never on daily suppression. Last flare she thinks was spring.
OB: G1P1, one vaginal birth in 2017, no complications. No surgeries.
Meds: valacyclovir 500 mg BID x3 days PRN prodrome.
Allergies: none to medications.
FHx: mother had a C-section; one sister also has recurrent HSV-2; maternal aunt with osteoporosis. No early heart disease or cancers she knows of.
Social: married, one child at home. Never smoked. Wine once or twice a month.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No genital exam today, she has no active lesions. Skin clear. Mood and affect normal.
PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P
1. Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hep C screening, she agrees. Pap/HPV per old records (believes 2021, normal); will confirm when chart arrives. Flu and COVID boosters next month when the fall supply is in.
2. Recurrent genital HSV: continue episodic valacyclovir; discussed daily suppression as an option if flares get more frequent. She prefers episodic. Message us for refills.

RTC yearly, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your results from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Grace, everything from Tuesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol are all in the normal range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Nothing to do. Good to meet you.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - LABOR & DELIVERY
Discharge Summary
Admitted 01/08/2024 04:40   Discharged 01/10/2024 12:15
Patient: Grace Paquette   DOB 11/02/1992

Admission: G2P1001 at 39w0d in spontaneous labor. Prenatal course without complications.

Hospital course: Labor advanced slowly but steadily. In the second stage she pushed for several hours with the vertex low and engaged and descent minimal. Given maternal fatigue and a tight perineum, an episiotomy was cut as the head crowned. She delivered a liveborn infant spontaneously at 13:58; no forceps or vacuum were used. Infant scores 8 and 9 at one and five minutes.

About four hours after delivery she told nursing she could not feel when she needed to move her bowels and had one episode of leaking stool. On examination the episiotomy had extended past its intended margin into the external anal sphincter; the rectal mucosa was intact. Assessed as a third-degree perineal laceration. Taken to the OR at 20:15 and the external anal sphincter was repaired under her epidural, with layered closure of the perineum.

Recovery thereafter was routine. Voiding without difficulty, passing soft stool by day 2, pain controlled with oral analgesics. Hemoglobin on postpartum day 1 acceptable.

Discharge diagnoses: term vaginal delivery; third-degree perineal laceration (external anal sphincter injury), repaired. Recurrent genital HSV, no lesions this admission.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge instructions: high-fiber diet and fluids; avoid straining; sitz baths. Referral placed to pelvic floor physical therapy. Postpartum visit in 6 weeks with our office.

cc: Primary care

documents.title: Post-delivery check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after discharge summary came in. Baby doing well, she's sore but up and around. Bowels moving. Still occasionally can't hold gas and had one small leak of stool this week - OB told her to expect this early on. PT eval scheduled for next Wed. No fever, incision not opening as far as she can tell, bleeding tapering. Mood good, sleeping in bits. Knows to call OB for fever, worsening pain or any foul discharge. Postpartum f/u with us in late Feb.

documents.title: Pelvic floor physical therapy: initial evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
PELVIC HEALTH PHYSICAL THERAPY
Initial evaluation 01/24/2024

Referral: obstetrics, s/p third-degree perineal laceration with sphincter repair 01/08/2024.
Subjective: 16 days postpartum. Reduced awareness of rectal filling, occasional flatus she cannot hold back, one small episode of stool leakage since discharge. No urinary leakage.
Objective (external exam only at this stage): perineum healing, sutures intact. Gentle voluntary contraction present, reduced endurance.
Assessment: postpartum anal sphincter weakness after obstetric injury, good prognosis.
Plan: biweekly visits x 8; graded pelvic floor strengthening, coordination and urge-deferral training; bowel habit education.

Physical therapist

documents.title: Obstetrics: postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS GROUP
Postpartum visit 02/19/2024

Ms. Paquette is six weeks out from a vaginal delivery complicated by a third-degree laceration, repaired. Perineum well healed; anal sphincter intact and contracting on exam. Stool leakage has become rare and she is in pelvic floor PT. Bleeding has stopped. Mood screen negative.

Counseled that the sphincter injury should be considered when planning any future delivery. Resume usual activity as tolerated.
No medication changes.

Obstetrics attending

documents.title: Postpartum Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seven weeks after delivery (01/08, vaginal, episiotomy extended into a 3rd-degree tear, sphincter repaired same night - see L&D summary). OB postpartum visit last week was fine.

She's doing PT every other week and doing the exercises at home. Leakage was a few times in the first two weeks, nothing in the past 10 days. Can sense the urge again. No urinary symptoms. Tired but okay; husband home evenings. PHQ-9 3. Back to school after spring break.

No HSV flare since fall 2022.

Exam: Looks well. Heart/lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Deferred perineal exam, done by OB last week.

A/P
1. Obstetric anal sphincter injury, repaired - recovering well with PT. Keep it on the problem list; it matters for any future delivery. Call if leakage comes back.
2. Postpartum - mood fine. CBC today; she was told her count was a little low after delivery.
3. HSV - episodic valacyclovir as before.
Physical in the fall.

REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - LABOR & DELIVERY
Discharge Summary
Admitted 01/01/2025 09:20   Discharged 01/04/2025 11:40
Patient: Grace Paquette   DOB 11/02/1992

Presentation: 32-year-old G3P2002 at 39w0d with contractions every five minutes for the past two hours. About a week ago painful blisters appeared on the vulva. She has known recurrent genital herpes, quiet for more than a year, and took no antiviral prophylaxis in this pregnancy. Pregnancy otherwise routine. Her first birth was vaginal; her second (01/2024) was vaginal with a repaired third-degree laceration.

On arrival: T 37.2 C (99.0 F), BP 120/78. Fetal tracing category I.
Exam: clusters of vesicles and shallow ulcerations over both labia majora. Speculum exam: cervix free of lesions. Lesion swab sent for HSV PCR; HSV-2 detected.

Course: With active genital lesions in labor, cesarean delivery was recommended and she agreed. Primary low transverse cesarean under spinal anesthesia; liveborn infant handed to the newborn team. Uncomplicated surgery and recovery. She restarted her own valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily for 3 days on postoperative day 1 for the outbreak; lesions crusting at discharge.

Discharge diagnoses: term pregnancy delivered by primary low transverse cesarean; active genital HSV at term (HSV-2). History of third-degree laceration, healed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: incision check 2 weeks, postpartum visit 6 weeks.

cc: Primary care

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to let us know - baby came 1/1 by C-section because she had an outbreak when labor started. Home since Saturday. Finished the 3 days of valacyclovir, sores almost gone. Incision sore, no redness or drainage, no fever. Walking around the house. Hospital will send summary. Postpartum appt with PCP set for Feb.

Exam: Well. Low transverse incision healed, no erythema. Abdomen soft. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P

2. Hx 3rd-degree laceration 2024 - stable, no symptoms.
3. S/p cesarean - healing well.
Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Labor and delivery / ICU discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - LABOR & DELIVERY
Discharge Summary
Admitted 01/01/2026 01:50   Discharged 01/05/2026 11:30
Patient: Grace Paquette   DOB 11/02/1992

Admission: 33-year-old G4P3003 at 39w0d in spontaneous labor, attempting a trial of labor after one prior low transverse cesarean (01/2025, for active HSV). Other births vaginal (2017; 01/2024 with a repaired third-degree laceration). Recurrent genital HSV, no lesions on admission. Uncomplicated pregnancy. NKDA. Admission hemoglobin 12.1.

Course: Contractions every 2 to 3 minutes. She reached complete dilation and had been at 10 cm with the vertex at +1 station for about an hour when the fetal heart rate fell abruptly from a baseline of 140 to 60 and did not recover for more than 3 minutes. At the same time she reported sudden, sharp lower abdominal pain. The uterus was firm, tense and tender; vaginal bleeding was minimal. Uterine rupture suspected and emergency cesarean called.

Operative findings: rupture through the prior low transverse scar with hemoperitoneum. Liveborn infant delivered and handed to the neonatal team. The uterine defect was repaired in two layers; the uterus was preserved. Estimated blood loss 1,700 mL. Two units of packed red cells transfused.

Postoperative: transferred to the ICU for overnight monitoring after the hemorrhage; hemodynamically stable, hemoglobin 7.8 after surgery. Transferred to postpartum floor 01/02. Ambulating, tolerating diet, incision clean. Hemoglobin 8.6 on 01/05.

Discharge diagnoses: uterine rupture during trial of labor after cesarean; emergency repeat cesarean with repair of uterine rupture; acute blood loss requiring transfusion. Recurrent genital HSV.
Discharge medications: ferrous sulfate 325 mg by mouth once daily for 3 months.
Counseling: any future pregnancy must be delivered by planned cesarean before the onset of labor; she should not labor again. Recommend early prenatal care if she conceives.
Follow-up: incision check 1 to 2 weeks; postpartum visit with CBC at 6 weeks.

cc: Primary care

documents.title: Outside records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hospital summary reviewed: TOLAC 1/1 ended in uterine rupture at the old scar, emergency cesarean and repair, uterus kept, 2 u PRBC, a night in the ICU. Hgb 8.6 at discharge, on iron per OB. OB following postpartum. Filed. Will reach out to her.

documents.title: Checking in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Grace, I read the hospital summary and I'm so sorry it was such a frightening delivery. I hope you and the baby are settling in at home. OB will see you for the incision and your six-week visit and recheck your blood count. Once you're up to it, I'd like to see you here too - no rush, just let the front desk know.

documents.title: RE: Checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you, that means a lot. We're home and doing okay - still pretty wiped out and the incision is sore but getting better every day. Taking the iron. I'll call once things calm down.

documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS GROUP
Postpartum visit 02/10/2026

Ms. Paquette is six weeks after emergency cesarean with repair of a uterine rupture. Incision well healed. Lochia resolved. Energy improving. Hemoglobin today 11.0, up from 8.6 at discharge; finish the 3-month iron course.

We again reviewed that any future pregnancy requires a scheduled cesarean before labor begins and early prenatal care.
Mood screen negative. Cleared for usual activity.

Obstetrics attending
